newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank - no plan for capital rise soon.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank - no plan for capital rise soon.

text.p: Commerzbank AG said on Tuesday its move to seek authorised capital did not imply that it planned a capital increase in the near future.
"We beg for this to be understood as a purely precautionary measure," chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen told a news conference.
"We have absolutely no fresh intention to go to the capital market," he said.
Commerzbank -no plan for capital rise soon
Earlier, Kohlhaussen had said he was confident the bank did not face any takeover threat.
"Many of you have been writing that Commerzbank should be worrying about its independence. But there is no evidence at all to back this up."
He noted that Commerzbank's market capitalisation had trebled in the last four years to reach 18.22 billion marks ($10.6 billion) on April 4, making the bank prohibitively expensive.
"Can you name me anyone that can afford this price?" Kohlhaussen said.
In its 1996 annual report, Commerzbank said a shareholder survey carried out in early 1997 did not detect any concentration of blocks of shares in the hands of individual investors.

About 40 percent of the bank's capital remained with foreign investors while the percentage of institutional investors remained virtually unchanged at 51 percent compared with previous years, the bank said.
Commerzbank on Monday announced it would ask for shareholder approval for possible future capital raising measures up to April 30, 2002.
Shareholders will be asked to authorise a 200 million-mark share issue as well as a 50 million-mark share issue for employees.
Approval will also be requested for up to two billion marks worth of profit-sharing certificates as well as up to one billion marks worth of bonds with warrants and options.
